comment: As a long time owner (1983) of Deer Valley's second community, Aspen Wood, I continue to be interested in all things Park City. Having watched yesterday's Council meeting with the Deer Valley representatives, I am left with several comments and questions pertaining to transportation. I will refer to those "events" which particularly impact Aspen Wood and leave the other communities to their own battles. 1. While it's unfortunate that a traffic light seems to be proposed for the Y intersection (just before Deer Valley Plaza), I do believe that in view of everything it may make traffic run more smoothly, especially if (and if I read the drawing correctly) vehicles turning right from Deer Valley Drive North may have a clear lane to turn right toward the rotary. End of ski day traffic on Deer Valley Drive South (The DV reps keep referring to it as Deer Valley Drive West-don't know where that came from.) has for several years now been a nightmare. I do, however, seriously doubt that will improve with this new development and will undoubtedly be worse. The thought that skiers will apres longer, therefore spreading departures over a longer period, is questionable. 2. And this is an important one, and one your Council will have control over: I gather that Deer Valley Drive South where it abuts the Aspen Wood property is 10' wide, where 12' is the minimum requirement for a three-lane road-one shared bus/bike lane and two travel lanes going in opposite directions. How is this extra footage acquired? We have a lovely sidewalk, used in both directions-towards DV and into town, a great amenity for our community. I would certainly be opposed to anything altering the dimensions of that, or Aspen Wood property. You have a long and stressful situation ahead of you as you make these important decisions for Park City. But, having listened to your thoughtful inquiries of the DV representatives, I trust you to arrive at the most feasible solution. Too bad the 1978 permit allowing use of this property didn't have a long-ago expiration date!
source: eComment (written; published verbatim in council meeting minutes)
